messages:
maria: seeing a spike in pod restarts in northern-eu GPU pool, jobs queuing, some 502s reported. rolling a quick check now.
jonah: on it — looking at autoscaler logs, might be OOM or driver glitch. @sre-oncall can you take node health?
sre-oncall: taking node health. early signs: /var/log shows nvidia driver reset on a subset of nodes. marking pool as degraded.
karthik: what's impact on customers? need a concise status page blurb if it's > partial outage.
maria: traffic to northern-eu currently ~18% of prod. recommend shifting new allocations to eu-west1 and eu-central1 for 30m. can we do a soft route?
jonah: I can push routing policy to shift new allocations only (no migrations). will add fallback to dedicated spare pool. applying policy: `route-policy apply --region northern-eu --shift-to eu-west1,eu-central1 --mode new-only`
deploy-bot: route-policy job queued: id=rp-3124. ETA 60s.
jonah: applied. new allocations should avoid northern-eu. monitoring queue length.
eva: support: customers A and B opened tickets with 502s, escalating. drafting status page. suggest: 'Partial service disruption in Northern EU affecting new pods and short-lived requests; mitigations in progress; ETA 45-60 minutes.'
statusbot: Incident created: INC-2026-NEU-GPU-1 — status: investigating. Subscribers notified.
sre-oncall: I've cordoned 6 nodes with driver resets and restarted node-driver services. kernel logs show `nvidia: GPU reinitialized` repeatedly. diag script output: ```/usr/local/bin/gpu-health-check --node n-023 -> driver-reset count: 7```
karthik: good. any cost impact from the routing shift? traffic to eu-west1 may spin up extra capacity.
maria: we'll hit burst capacity in eu-west1; expected delta ~$1.2k/hr if sustained. notifying finance and product.
support: I've pushed the status draft and posted to https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-NEU-GPU-1. Included ETA 60m and contact link. Customers B and C updated via support channel.
jonah: queue length down ~40% after shift. patching nodes now: updating GPU driver to 525.85 and restarting kubelet.
sre-oncall: one node failed to rejoin; collecting logs and opening a support ticket with cloud provider. tagging `networking` and `storage` in ticket.
eva: Can we prepare an ETA update in 30 mins? I'll include whether routing is still in effect. Also mention possible increased latency for customers routed to eu-west1.
maria: :thumbsup: I'll monitor token throughput and let you know if we need wider shift.
statusbot: Update INC-2026-NEU-GPU-1: mitigations applied, new allocations routed away from Northern EU. Investigation ongoing. Next update in 30m or on major change.
support: Customer D replied upset about higher latency. Escalating to account team — @karthik can you loop in sales for high-touch customers?
karthik: looped sales. they'll send a personal note. also proposing a temporary credit for affected customers — product ok with <$2k threshold?
eva: I approved communications for <2k credits. log decisions in incident doc.
maria: final note: if driver patch fails on more than 10% of nodes, we switch to full region drain and route all traffic out. current affected nodes 7/120 (~5.8%).
jonah: agree. for now continue soft-shift. will post when queue normalized or if requeues spike.
sre-oncall: collecting final logs, will attach to incident. I'm running `kubectl get pods -n redwood --field-selector=status.phase=Pending` to watch backlog.
deploy-bot: route-policy rp-3124: success.
statusbot: INC-2026-NEU-GPU-1 update: routing applied successfully, backlog decreasing. ETA remains 60m.
maria: :wave: thanks team — monitoring, will post update at T+30.
